INTERFACE_MANAGER.note: jag::InterfaceManager. Settled on 949-5 as ONE object behind what were three separate names. Evidence, all on the target: it is the `this` the LoginProtocolHandler passes at two sites to the per-tick routine that clears the key-event vector and refills it from the recorder ring; it is the `this` of EnterTargetMode/LeaveTargetMode, which write and clear the target-mode trio (active flag, verb string, target-name string); and it is the base if_find does `ADD 0x30` on to reach the component container. ~200 loads, almost all if_*/cc_* opcode handlers and interface packet handlers. The key-event vector ClientProt::FlushPerTick drains is a member of THIS object, so the former OClient.INPUT_EVENT_VIEW was this same field under a type name that does not exist. Leaf function names in this family are not all attested - identification here rests on the behaviour, not on them.

CHILD_ARRAY_BEGIN.note: EASTL vector triple at parent+0x8: { begin, end, capacity }. Each element is 0x18 bytes: byte 0 = "removed" flag (0 = live slot), bytes 0x10..0x17 = shared_ptr value (the InterfaceComponent pointer). Derived from jag::InterfaceManager::DrawComponentList @ 0x00428480 — the loop reads *(char*)(elem+0) for the live check and *(void**)(elem+0x10) for the component pointer, stepping by 0x18 from begin to end. | 949-1

PARENT_LAYER_ID.note: ushort parent-layer component id; 0xffff = no parent layer. Indexes the InterfaceParent child-slot array (stride 0x18, component shared_ptr at slot+0x10). NOT a component type: the CS2 component type is consumed by the InterfaceComponent factory to pick the C++ subclass and is never written back onto the object.

FLAGS.note: Bitfield. Bit 0x20 = visible flag (set/cleared by jag::game::InterfaceComponent::SetVisibleFlag @ 0x00216600). Other bits (e.g. 0x04, 0x08) are not yet decoded.

Y_ORIGIN_MODE.note: byte: same semantics as X_ORIGIN_MODE for vertical axis

Y_ANCHOR_MODE.note: byte: same semantics as X_ANCHOR_MODE for vertical axis

RAW_WIDTH.note: int: unanchored WIDTH input, fed through X_ANCHOR_MODE into SCREEN_WIDTH by Layer::LayoutChild. Position comes from X_ORIGIN_OFFSET via X_ORIGIN_MODE, not from here

RAW_HEIGHT.note: int: unanchored HEIGHT input, fed through Y_ANCHOR_MODE into SCREEN_HEIGHT

PARENT_REL_X.note: Parent-LOCAL position written each frame by the layout pass (Layer::LayoutChildren -> Layer::LayoutChild). NOT screen-absolute. Absolute X/Y is reconstructed each frame in jag::InterfaceManager::DrawComponentList by adding the slot's screen-absolute origin to these values; that data is ephemeral and only available via the INTERFACEMANAGER_DRAWCOMPONENTLIST hook (see hooks.impl.InterfaceComponentRectCapture). | 949-1 int: parent-local X within parent layer's interior coord system

MODEL_ID.note: int, -1 = none; config type-6 defaultMediaId / IF_SETMODEL target (GetModelId @0x172200)

MODEL_OBJECT.note: pointer, lazily-built model object, null until built

SLOT_CHILDREN.note: A component's child components are NOT a single vector at a fixed offset — a Layer stores them in a paged array at +0x1A0 (begin) / +0x1A8 (end), 0x68-byte page entries (see jag::game::Layer draw FUN_003eccd0). The canonical, flat way to reach every component is InterfaceParent's slot vector at +0x8, indexed by component id (InterfaceParent.get / the InterfaceList.getComponent path). There is no per-component CHILDREN vector; the old CHILDREN=0x178 was bogus (it overlapped ITEM_ID/STACK_SIZE and read them as a vector header). | vector<0x18>

EMPTY_CELL_SENTINEL_REL.note: Re-derived against 949-5: 0x1692a70 -> 0x1693a70. Read off LEA RAX,[0x1693a70] in jag::game::HeightMap::SampleRegionFineHeight at four independent sites; sibling returns are B+4 and B+8. NAME IS MISLEADING: the _REL suffix means module-relative, not a struct displacement, and the target is not a heightmap-private sentinel - it is a shared 4-entry int32 pool {0,1,2,3} in .bss written once by a global ctor and returned as a const int* by ~100 unrelated functions. SHOW_AS_IMPORTANT.note: Boolean (byte) — "show as important" flag. MENU_OPEN.note: Non-zero only while a right-click menu is open. OPOBJ folds it into the trailing flags byte: set => server picks up immediately ("Take"); clear => server opens the area-loot interface.

CLIENT.note: jag::Client* the send callback reads out of its `this`. Verified in DoOpWalk @0x161b30, which opens with `lVar3 = *param_1` and reaches every manager through it. Windows keeps the same field at +0x8.

CLICK_BUFFER_WRITE.note: Renamed from the previous HEAD/TAIL pair, which had the roles inverted. Verified in SendEventMouseClick and in the movement ring's pop and producer: the first dword after the slots is the WRITE cursor, the second is the READ cursor, and a ring is empty when they are equal.

CLICK_BUFFER_READ.note: Renamed from the previous HEAD/TAIL pair, which had the roles inverted. Verified in SendEventMouseClick and in the movement ring's pop and producer: the first dword after the slots is the WRITE cursor, the second is the READ cursor, and a ring is empty when they are equal.

MOVE_BUFFER_BASE.note: Movement ring, distinct from the click ring. Read off PopEventMouseMoveSample's slot LEA and corroborated by the producer, which writes at the same array through the recorder sub-object.

MOVE_BUFFER_WRITE.note: First dword after the 200 slots. The producer writes the slot it indexes then advances this.

MOVE_BUFFER_READ.note: Second dword after the slots. PopEventMouseMoveSample advances this on every pop, including samples the sender then elides.

MOVE_BUFFER_CAPACITY.note: 200 slots; the pop wraps above 199 and the producer wraps above 199.

MOVE_ENTRY_SIZE.note: Same 40-byte MouseSample as the click ring.

X.note: Was transposed with Y in this table. SendEventMouseClick builds the position word as (slot[+8] << 16) | slot[+4] and the wire is little-endian, so slot[+4] leaves first and is X; the movement producer likewise stores its first float argument at slot[+4].

XP_IN_TENTHS.note: Single BYTE at +0x8 (the three bytes above it are padding the client never initialises -- read them and the flag is spurious). Non-zero when the client tracks this skill's experience in TENTHS of an xp point, which is how it represents progress past the 200,000,000 cap (the stored value then caps at 2,000,000,000). StatTable::UpdateStat stores the wire value raw and divides by 10 for the level lookup, so a reader that ignores this flag reports 10x the real experience once it is set. Normal accounts run with it clear -- the plain stat_xp opcode returns the stored value unscaled.

BOUNDS_MIN_X.note: Current transformed AABB (axis-aligned bounding box) Stored as two SSE-aligned float4 vectors in raw {X, Z, Y} memory order (same axis layout as scene position at 0xF0/0xF4/0xF8)

SRC_BOUNDS_MIN_X.note: 0x5C = marker (-1.0) Source/untransformed AABB (same {X, Z, Y} layout)

LOCAL_X.note: 0x7C = src marker Local position (before parent accumulation)

SCENE_X.note: Scene position (accumulated world position = local + parent chain)

PICK_TYPE.note: Screen-space picking data (populated by render pipeline, used by ScenePicker::TestEntityHit) | int: 0=point/circle, non-zero=line segment

ANIMATION_SHARED_PTR.note: Base of the animation slot's active shared_ptr; the object word is at +0x8. jag::game::AnimatedModel::ServiceAnimationLoading @0x691790 swaps pending into active as {ctrl slot+0x20, obj slot+0x28} with the slot based at entity+0xa80.

objectNotes.doActions: 66 DoActions total, all registered by ONE function on Linux: the jag::MiniMenu ctor FUN_00078b4e installs every sender inline (there is no second component-action registrar as there is on Windows). Action object layout: +0x00 client ctx, +0x10 invoker thunk, +0x18 sender fn (all three written at runtime by the ctor), +0x20 dispatch id, +0x24 kind (both written by the static initializer FUN_000af050). Layout re-derived from this binary and validated by reproducing five already-correct rows exactly before any change: SELECT_NPC 8, WALK 23, DIALOGUE 30, SELECT_TILE 59, and COMPONENT 57 / COMPONENT_SIXPLUS 1007 sharing one sender. LOC FAMILY CORRECTED 2026-07: the loc rows were mis-paired, every name sitting one slot below its true sender, which left OBJECT_4 with no address at all (0x0, so DoActionOpcode.OBJECT_4.fire() was a no-op). True kind-3 mapping is id 1 SELECT_OBJECT 0x162af0, 2 OBJECT_1 0x162bc0, 3 OBJECT_2 0x162ba0, 4 OBJECT_3 0x162b80, 5 OBJECT_4 0x162b60, 1001 OBJECT_5 0x162b40, 1002 OBJECT_6 0x162b20. SELECT_OBJECT's sender was previously absent from the table entirely; it is the only loc sender that branches on jag::g_protocolRevision (descriptor DAT_016844b0 = ClientProt op 9 size 17 below 0x3b5, else DAT_01683e10 = op 116 size 18) and the only one SendOpLoc special-cases to also emit the pending selection state, and FUN_001cdfa0 groups its action object with the other select-family objects (SELECT_TILE, SELECT_NPC, SELECT_GROUND_ITEM, PLAYER_SELECT, COMP_ON_PLAYER, SELECT_COMPONENT_ITEM) and no other loc action. Each of DoOpLoc1..6 dispatches a distinct fixed-size-9 ClientProt op (41, 70, 33, 91, 1, 88), so a wrong pairing would have sent the wrong in-game action rather than failing loudly. ALIAS IDS: Linux has the same alias-copy pattern as Windows - the ctor calls FUN_00cbee00(dst,src) to copy a registered object's callable into a second object under another id, giving loc 1001/1002 also as 6/7 (recorded as OBJECT_5_ALT/OBJECT_6_ALT), npc 2009-2013/3003 also as 9-13/1003, player 44-53 also as 2044-2053. Which id of a pair the client actually dispatches at runtime is UNKNOWN and matters only for DoActionOpcode.getActionById; no existing row's id was flipped between members of a pair. Next lead for that: capture real menu clicks on a 5-op and a 6-op loc and read the dispatched id.

objectNotes.ONPC: CURRENT_HP/MAX_HP hold a 0-100 health RATIO, not absolute hitpoints — the NXT client is only told the headbar proportion. Verified live on 949-1: Man, Cow, Skoblin and Guard all read 100/100 at full health, with every neighbouring dword zero, so the values are deliberate rather than garbage. A displacement scan of .text finds no direct dword access at either offset; the write goes through the update-mask handler's computed pointer. Do not 'correct' these to absolute HP on that scan alone — still unconfirmed is whether they track damage, which needs an NPC observed at partial health.
